first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates simpler onboarding durably improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing may address competitive pressure but has documented 30-day retention harm, which conflicts with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Verify the core onboarding result and the pricing trade-off before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a simplified-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and the linked 6% activation decline, with confirmed evidence of +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention. Promotional pricing is not selected because its confirmed retention loss conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue despite short-term acquisition gains.

final2.rationale: Keep the simplified-onboarding experiment. It has confirmed durable improvements in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, and directly addresses the concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn create an urgent retention risk, but the only pricing evidence available shows that targeted discounts produce a cohort that fails to sustain through renewal; it does not establish that discounting will defensibly retain the current SMB base. Pricing pressure should be monitored as a material unresolved risk rather than answered with an unproven, value-destructive discount experiment this cycle.
